entry.title: Disenfranchisement in Spatial Voting Games
entry.summary:
The questions of voting rights, group membership, and the boundaries of acceptable discourse all involve a recursive, self-stability issue, wherein the voters, group members, and acceptable commentators are often the ultimate arbiters of their own rules for inclusion and exclusion. In order to understand how ideological or issue diversity may impact the stability of such inclusion and exclusion, we introduce franchise elections, where voting members of a group vote to change the electorate. In particular, when agents are positioned inside an ideological or issue space, a social choice function that aggregates agent viewpoints induces a preference for agents over group composition, where agents prefer groups that improve the social choice function outcome for them.

Source: arXiv Economics (econ.EM, econ.GN, econ.TH) · Tags: #econometrics #macroeconomics #decision-theory #market-design

entry.title: A Push Down the Mountain: Framing Effects and Internal State Interventions on Collusive Behavior in a Long-Horizon LLM Agent
entry.summary:
Can sustained gain-loss (valence) framing sway an LLM agent toward market manipulation? We place Gemma 3 12B into the seat of a defendant in the London silver-fixing litigation, in a market simulation built from real case transcripts. Across 260 simulations, the agent is asked to collude on the price of silver by a counterparty.

Source: arXiv Economics (econ.EM, econ.GN, econ.TH) · Tags: #econometrics #macroeconomics #ml-theory #llm

entry.title: Learning Dynamics of the Influencer's Game in Resource Landscapes
entry.summary:
Across domains as varied as ecology, economics, and online platforms, individuals are incentivized to position themselves within resource-rich strategy spaces. In this work we introduce a new spatial game framework called the influencer's game. Within this new framework players' strategies are represented as positions within a trait space.

entry.title: Unequal Rewards and the Direction of Scientific Work: Evidence from U.S. Public Universities
entry.summary:
Research on pay dispersion has long asked whether unequal rewards increase or depress performance. Tournament theory expects stronger effort, while social comparison accounts expect withdrawal. Both perspectives, however, treat performance as a single scale on which workers can be ranked.

entry.title: Accuracy Is Not Welfare: Evaluating AI Buyers under Strategic Price Complexity in a Synthetic Duopoly
entry.summary:
AI buying agents may alter sellers' incentives as well as consumers' decisions. In a synthetic duopoly, we evaluate price-comparison pipelines on a fixed menu and in empirical correlated-equilibrium games. Calculator assistance selects an optimal offer 84.00% of the time, versus 68.57% under verified-total disclosure, yet disclosure has a 20.14-unit higher consumer-worst equilibrium surplus.

Source: arXiv Economics (econ.EM, econ.GN, econ.TH) · Tags: #econometrics #macroeconomics #decision-theory #quant-finance

entry.title: How Will the 340B Rebate Model Pilot Affect Covered Entity Finances? -- by Charles J. Courtemanche
entry.summary:
The Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA) plans to implement a pilot switching 340B from an upfront discount model to a rebate model for drugs in the Medicare Drug Price Negotiation Program (MDPNP). This study uses calibration methods to predict the impact of the rebate model pilot (RMP) on covered entities’ net revenues from the 340B program. I examine possible losses from averted duplicate discounts; denial of valid claims; manufacturers using data to exert influence; liquidity-related expenses; and administrative and staffing costs.

Source: NBER Working Papers (National Bureau of Economic Research) · Tags: #macroeconomics #econometrics

entry.title: Horizontal Equity of Taxation: Citizen Beliefs and Policy Preferences -- by Pierre Bachas, Christopher A. Hoy, Anders Jensen, Mahvish Shaukat
entry.summary:
Taxes are harder to enforce on the self-employed than on wage earners, creating horizontal inequities among taxpayers with similar incomes. Using tax microsimulation and household survey data from 29 developing countries, we show that horizontal inequities in actual tax systems are comparable in magnitude to vertical equity and are exacerbated by progressive reforms that fall disproportionately on wage earners. We then conduct surveys and randomized information experiments in Pakistan to study public perceptions of these inequities.

Source: NBER Working Papers (National Bureau of Economic Research) · Tags: #macroeconomics #econometrics

entry.title: Monetary policy in a Phelps–Winter Economy -- by Bruce C. Greenwald, Joseph E. Stiglitz
entry.summary:
We use the Phelps-Winter customer market—providing a better theory of price determination for large parts of the economy than the standard model—to show that raising interest rates induces higher prices, as firms value current profits more, and are more willing to lose customers for short-term gains. These inflationary effects can be significant in relevant ranges of interest rates; they exist in the short run even when interest rate hikes succeed in cutting aggregate demand; and that they are amplified by policy uncertainty and the uncertainty about the effects of interest rate changes, both of which have increased as conventional policy has demonstrably failed badly to keep inflation at the 2% target. Empirical studies confirm this low level of ineffectiveness of raising interest rates in reducing inflation.

Source: NBER Working Papers (National Bureau of Economic Research) · Tags: #macroeconomics #econometrics

entry.title: Measuring the Impact of Impact Measurement -- by Emanuele Colonnelli, Timothy McQuade, Natalia Rigol, Benjamin N. Roth
entry.summary:
Impact measurement is central to impact investing and social entrepreneurship, yet little is known about whether firms benefit privately from measuring impact. We conduct the first randomized controlled trial of an impact measurement intervention among high-growth social enterprises in India. Treated firms exhibit nearly twice as much revenue growth and raise nearly twice as much capital as control firms.

Source: NBER Working Papers (National Bureau of Economic Research) · Tags: #macroeconomics #econometrics
